title: Complete all-size logical BIT caller and recursive storage bound
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

[PR #2697](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2697) executes the selected BIT caller only for `64 <= n < 128`, where every child is a leaf. This package implements whole-packet recursive entry/return for every internal width, preserving the child's independent unused row stock, exact ordered gap/spectators, frozen source fields and serialized coefficient program. An iterative scheduler avoids a host recursion-depth restriction. A linear sign implementation removes a hidden per-column precision factor, and all descendants share the fixed source tables instead of retaining a new cached topology after every return.

The written endpoint/stock induction is paired with a complete logical live-symbol ledger, including numerical/control/count/directory contents and suspended parents: `< 11 V_root + F_q` under the explicit canonical root coupling. This is a source-level construction with the baseline `p=1` time recurrence. It does **not** establish fixed-physical-tape lowering, the stronger selected H2 contracts, the outer borrowing wrapper or a new κ. The selected frontier is unchanged.

Everything is scoped to `research/selected-bit-recursive-caller/`. Read its README, PROOF, exact source manifests and VALIDATION record. Frozen predecessor files and the selected result are untouched.

## Task and overlap

Task `selected-stock-envelope`, priority revision 5, refined by an explicit request for a central implementation bottleneck. Started from canonical main `7b39515117fe26e75d16c268877391f1bdaa5640` at 19:19:46 UTC. The submission refresh checked main `63a279f5790872996a13f0e9efdae35818171b48`; guidance, selected record and every live input were unchanged. Full overlap pagination covered 727 open PRs and 1,382 Discussion/comment/reply records without warnings.

The executable predecessor is Jose Manuel's [PR #2697](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2697) at `a53fdf4bcbe33c6732f0bec1badc8c023380f9d1`. Its 50 exported files are authenticated before import. Exact source pins also retain [PR #2234](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2234)'s compatible stock/profile chain and the [PR #2688](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2688), [PR #2708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2708), [PR #2731](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2731) component storage proofs.

A matching [recursive-boundary claim by jmbarrancoml](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2319#discussioncomment-18957230) appeared at 19:47 UTC, after this work began. This is an independent implementation and joined logical-reserve argument; no exclusive novelty is claimed. Nick Petalas's [PR #2743](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2743) (`c1e8065671f4f1854c5508f4bb18b85851074547`) supplies a sharper first-range payload/key result, which is not claimed as new here. The finer first-range count component was published during validation as [PR #2749](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2749) (`a18ba3bbfb549af66488a890edcb4a3744de90a3`) and is likewise separate. TASK.json records the scope and timing rather than asserting that metadata searches prove novelty.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-recursive-caller
```

**All five registered suites passed locally in 520.413 seconds; a separate before/after SHA256 inventory confirmed that all 84 package files were unchanged.** The suites compare complete typed receipts and authenticate 11 live inputs, 50 executable predecessor files and four proof/notice exports. Evidence includes:

- 7,843,392 selected literal caller events and the full provider catalogue.
- A complete 15,552-column GL2 Boolean model, including COPY, IDLE, bridge/exchange, all 672 residual calls and 5,712 child returns.
- A true two-level 9,216-address toy with 12 real internal returns and all six GL2 child classes. The root uses coordinate projectors; its children execute the full conjugated good/fallback forms. This q=2 toy is not selected GL64 execution.
- Independently derived ordered child layouts; actual remainder peeling above the old range; selected descriptor/frame handoffs `256 -> 168 -> 84` with explicitly controlled tiny child consumers; 1,501 scheduler frames; and shared source-table cache checks.
- Missing/duplicate/mutated return, aborted child, failed constructor, sign counter-cost, stale-state, invalid-stock, source-pin and exact-receipt controls.

The finite checks support the parametric proof; they do not enumerate the enormous selected GL64 payload. No selected cold replay, physical compiler, proof-assistant result or human review is claimed. Verification is read-only; explicit receipt generation refuses overwrite.

## Credit

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`) and the retained NOTICE supply the selected source/caller/normal-form/grammar lineage. Credit starship-s's [PR #2731](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2731) residual lifetime proof, Nick Petalas's [PR #2708](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2708) routing and [PR #2743](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2743) caller payload work, and ywz65's [PR #2688](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2688) directory reserve. Pending parallel work remains credited and provisional. Apache-2.0; substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including mathematical and implementation-checking subagents.

## Open next questions

The package lists three concrete follow-ups: serialize and price the logical caller on the required fixed physical tapes; improve the actual O(wV) route/leaf implementations to the selected H2 contracts; and supply/restorably pad compatible stock through the outer borrowing wrapper. The present baseline can feed the inherited conditional ordinary-caller bootstrap once its physical and outer-wrapper premises are supplied.
